facts.raw_span: A 67-year-old woman
31-year history of recurrent depressive disorder
depressed mood, anhedonia, nervousness, fatigue, decreased appetite, and poor sleep
beginning 5 months after COVID-19
two severe episodes responsive to escitalopram (up to 20 mg/d) and duloxetine (up to 60 mg/d)
intolerance to venlafaxine, bupropion, and trazodone
mother had mania
denied iron deficiency anemia, hypothyroidism, or substance abuse
Physical and neurologic examinations and routine laboratory tests were unremarkable
new deep itching and creeping sensations in her bilateral shoulders and arms
worse at rest, partially relieved by movement, and predominantly occurring in the evening
causing night-time sleep disturbance

concepts.why: The patient has a 31-year history of recurrent depressive disorder with symptoms of depressed mood, anhedonia, and fatigue, which are characteristic of major depressive disorder.
The patient's new deep itching and creeping sensations in her bilateral shoulders and arms, worse at rest and partially relieved by movement, are consistent with restless legs syndrome.
The patient's depressive episode began 5 months after COVID-19, suggesting a possible link between the two conditions.

The patient has a history of two severe depressive episodes and has tried multiple medications, including escitalopram, duloxetine, venlafaxine, bupropion, and trazodone, with limited success, indicating treatment-resistant depression.
The patient's mother had mania, which increases the patient's risk of developing bipolar disorder, although the patient's current symptoms are more consistent with major depressive disorder.
